description: Candidate set B: deliberately flawed, to exercise every failure mode the metrics are meant to catch. Specifically contains: (1) two false-positive supports of insufficient-evidence claims (C6, C8), (2) a missed hop in a multi-hop chain (C4, only 2 of 3 evidence items), (3) an accepted contradiction -- a contradicted claim wrongly marked supported (C10), (4) a correctly-abstained claim with incorrect/irrelevant cited evidence (C9), and (5) one 'novel' claim with no ground-truth counterpart (novel:extra1), to exercise the open-ended-generation code path.

claims.text: OrderService.create_order calls PaymentService.charge to process payment.
OrderService.create_order calls OrderRepository.save to persist the order.
OrderController transitively depends on the Order entity, via OrderService and OrderRepository.
claims._deliberate_error: MISSING the third hop (OrderRepository.save operates_on Order) -- the chain is incomplete. Should reduce evidence_completeness for this claim.

claims.text: OrderController transitively depends on PaymentService for payment processing, via OrderService.
OrderController requires the customer to be authenticated via OAuth2 before placing an order.
claims._deliberate_error: FALSE-POSITIVE support: ground truth is insufficient_evidence. The cited span is just the constructor storing order_service; it has nothing to do with authentication. This should count as an unsupported claim wrongly accepted.

claims.text: OrderService sends a confirmation email to the customer after placing an order.
PaymentService.charge performs fraud detection (risk scoring / anomaly analysis) on transactions before charging them.
claims._deliberate_error: FALSE-POSITIVE support: ground truth is insufficient_evidence (not contradicted -- see the corrected C8 in ground_truth/claims.json). The candidate cites the real charge() span but wrongly treats the absence of fraud-detection code as license to mark the claim 'supported', which is exactly the false-accept failure this metric suite is meant to catch (a second instance alongside C6).

claims.text: OrderRepository persists Order entities to a SQL database.
claims._deliberate_error: Status is correct (insufficient_evidence, matching the corrected ground truth) but the candidate hallucinates an IRRELEVANT cited span anyway (OrderService.create_order, not anything in OrderRepository, and ground truth expects zero evidence for this claim) -- should fail evidence_correctness even though the status matches, per evaluator/metrics.py's documented handling of evidence cited against an empty ground-truth expected_evidence list.

ACCEPTED CONTRADICTION: ground truth is contradicted -- the class statement's complete base list is {InMemoryRepository}, not SqlRepository. The candidate cites the right relationship (the real declared base) but draws the wrong conclusion from it, wrongly marking the claim supported.

claims.text: OrderService validates that the charge amount is positive before calling PaymentService.charge.
claims._deliberate_error: NOVEL claim with no ground-truth counterpart (also happens to be false -- create_order performs no such validation -- but the point of including it here is to exercise the 'claim_id not found in ground truth' path in the evaluator, which must exclude it from precision/recall rather than silently miscounting it).
